html:
The Huron, who call themselves Wendat, were a confederacy of Iroquoian-speaking peoples living between Lake Simcoe and Georgian Bay in what is now Ontario. The map's label covers a much wider area of the eastern Great Lakes in 1500.

They lived in palisaded towns of longhouses and grew maize, beans and squash. Their towns held tens of thousands of people in the early 1600s, and they were the middlemen of the fur trade, swapping maize and goods with northern hunters for furs they sold to the French. French Jesuits built the mission of Sainte-Marie among them in 1639.

Epidemics in the 1630s killed perhaps half of them. In 1648 and 1649 the Haudenosaunee destroyed their towns during the Beaver Wars, and the Wendat scattered. Some settled near Quebec City, at today's Wendake; others, joined with the Petun, became the Wyandot of Ohio, Kansas and Oklahoma. Their neighbours included the Neutral and the Algonquin.
